source: Hand-written for Terra Tempora; places and dates from standard references (see each event's links).

events.title: Temüjin is born
events.place: Delüün Boldog, on the Onon River (traditional site)
events.summary: The future Genghis Khan is born into the Borjigin clan, son of the chieftain Yesügei. The year is traditionally 1162, though 1155 and 1167 are also given. His father's murder when he was about nine left the family outcast, a hardship that shaped his rise.
events.search: Genghis Khan

events.title: Temüjin proclaimed Genghis Khan
events.place: Great assembly at the source of the Onon River
events.summary: Having united the Mongol and Turkic tribes of the steppe, Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan at a great assembly, a kurultai. He reorganises his people into units of ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand, and lays down the laws later known as the Yassa. The Mongol Empire dates from this moment.
events.search: Mongol empire

events.title: Siege of Yinchuan
events.place: Zhongxing (Yinchuan), capital of the Western Xia
events.summary: The Mongols besiege the Western Xia capital and try to flood it by diverting the Yellow River, but the dyke breaks and floods their own camp. Emperor Li Anquan submits all the same, paying tribute and giving a daughter in marriage. It is the Mongols' first conquest of a settled state.
events.search: Western Xia

events.title: Battle of Yehuling
events.place: Badger's Mouth pass, north-west of Zhangjiakou
events.summary: At the Badger's Mouth pass, Genghis Khan's army destroys a much larger army of the Jin dynasty. The defeat opens northern China to the Mongols and is remembered as one of the bloodiest battles of the age.
events.search: Jin dynasty Mongol

events.title: Fall of Zhongdu
events.summary: After the Jin court flees south to Kaifeng, the Mongols take and sack Zhongdu, the Jin capital on the site of today's Beijing. The Jin hold out in the south for almost twenty more years.
events.search: Zhongdu

events.title: Siege of Otrar
events.summary: The governor of Otrar had massacred a Mongol trade caravan, and the Khwarazm Shah had killed Genghis Khan's envoys. In revenge the Mongols invade Khwarazm and besiege Otrar, which falls after months; its governor is put to death.
events.search: Khwarezmian Empire Mongol invasion

events.title: Fall of Bukhara
events.summary: Genghis Khan crosses the Kyzylkum desert to appear behind the Khwarazmian lines and takes Bukhara. The city is sacked and burned; the Persian historian Juvayni has him tell its people that he is the punishment of God.
events.search: Bukhara

events.title: Fall of Samarkand
events.place: Samarkand, capital of the Khwarazm Shah
events.summary: Samarkand, the richest city of the Khwarazmian empire, surrenders after a short siege. Much of its garrison is killed and thousands of craftsmen are sent east to work for the Mongols.
events.search: Samarkand

events.title: Fall of Gurganj
events.summary: Gurganj, the old Khwarazmian capital, resists for months until the Mongols flood it by breaking the dams of the Amu Darya. Its fall is often counted among the bloodiest massacres in history.
events.search: Urgench

events.title: Battle of the Indus
events.summary: Genghis Khan catches Jalal al-Din, the last Khwarazmian prince, against the Indus and destroys his army. Jalal al-Din escapes by riding his horse off the bank into the river, a feat Genghis Khan is said to have admired.
events.search: Jalal al-Din Mingburnu

events.title: Battle of the Kalka River
events.place: Kalka River, north of the Sea of Azov
events.summary: On a long scouting raid around the Caspian, the generals Jebe and Subutai defeat an alliance of Rus princes and Cumans. The captured princes are crushed beneath a wooden platform on which the victors feast.
events.search: Battle of the Kalka River

events.title: Death of Genghis Khan
events.place: Liupan Mountains, during the war on the Western Xia
events.summary: Genghis Khan dies while his armies are destroying the Western Xia; whether from a fall from his horse, illness or a wound is unknown. He is buried in secret in Mongolia, and his grave has never been found.
events.search: Genghis Khan

events.title: Ögedei elected Great Khan
events.summary: At an assembly on the Kherlen River, Genghis Khan's third son Ögedei is confirmed as his successor. Under him the empire builds a capital and a network of relay stations, the yam, and resumes its wars in China, Persia and Europe.
events.search: Ögödei

events.title: Fall of the Jin at Caizhou
events.summary: Mongol and Southern Song armies besiege the last Jin emperor at Caizhou. Emperor Aizong hands the throne to a general and takes his own life, and the Jin dynasty ends in 1234.
events.search: Jin dynasty

events.title: Karakorum becomes the capital
events.summary: Ögedei walls Karakorum in the Orkhon valley and makes it the capital. Merchants, envoys and craftsmen from across Eurasia gather there; William of Rubruck later describes its silver tree, a fountain that poured four drinks.
events.search: Karakorum

events.title: Sack of Ryazan
events.place: Old Ryazan, on the Oka River
events.summary: Batu and Subutai open the invasion of the Rus principalities by storming Ryazan in December 1237. The city is destroyed and never rebuilt on that site.
events.search: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus

events.title: Fall of Vladimir
events.summary: The Mongols take Vladimir, the leading city of north-eastern Rus, in February 1238; the grand prince's family dies in the burning cathedral. A month later Grand Prince Yuri II is killed at the Sit River.
events.search: Vladimir-Suzdal

events.title: Fall of Kyiv
events.summary: Kyiv, the old capital of the Rus, falls in December 1240 after a short siege. Most of the city is destroyed, and the Mongols move on into Poland and Hungary.
events.search: Kyiv Mongol 1240

events.title: Battle of Legnica
events.summary: On 9 April 1241 a Mongol force sent to guard the flank defeats the Polish and Moravian knights of Duke Henry II the Pious, who is killed. Two days later the main army fights at Mohi.
events.search: Battle of Legnica

events.title: Battle of Mohi
events.place: Mohi, on the Sajó River, Hungary
events.summary: On the Sajó River, Batu and Subutai crush the army of King Béla IV of Hungary on 11 April 1241. Much of Hungary is ravaged over the following year.
events.search: Battle of Mohi

events.title: Death of Ögedei
events.summary: Ögedei dies in December 1241, reportedly after a night of heavy drinking. The princes leading the European campaign turn back for the succession, and the Mongols leave Hungary in 1242.
events.search: Ögödei

events.title: Battle of Köse Dağ
events.place: Köse Dağ, between Sivas and Erzincan
events.summary: The general Baiju defeats the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in eastern Anatolia. The Seljuks become Mongol vassals, paying tribute.
events.search: Seljuks of Rum Mongol

events.title: A papal envoy at Güyük's enthronement
events.place: Sira Ordo, the khan's camp near Karakorum
events.summary: Giovanni da Pian del Carpine, sent by Pope Innocent IV, witnesses Güyük's enthronement as Great Khan. Güyük's reply orders the Pope to come and submit; Carpini's report is one of the first European accounts of the Mongols.
events.search: Giovanni da Pian del Carpine

events.title: William of Rubruck at Karakorum
events.summary: The Flemish friar William of Rubruck reaches Möngke's court and spends months at Karakorum. He takes part in a debate between Christians, Muslims and Buddhists held before the khan, and leaves a vivid account of the city.
events.search: William of Rubruck

events.title: Sack of Baghdad
events.summary: Hülegü, Möngke's brother, besieges and sacks Baghdad. The caliph al-Musta'sim is put to death and the Abbasid caliphate ends, a blow long remembered across the Islamic world.
events.search: Siege of Baghdad 1258

events.title: Möngke dies at Diaoyu Fortress
events.summary: Möngke dies while besieging the Song fortress of Diaoyu, of disease or a wound. His death halts the campaigns in China and the Middle East as the princes go home to fight over the succession.
events.search: Möngke

events.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
events.summary: With most of Hülegü's army withdrawn after Möngke's death, the Mamluks of Egypt under Qutuz and Baybars defeat the Mongol force left in Syria. It is the first major Mongol defeat and stops their advance towards Egypt.
events.search: Battle of Ain Jalut

events.title: Kublai proclaimed khan; civil war
events.summary: Kublai is proclaimed Great Khan at Shangdu while his brother Ariq Böke claims the title at Karakorum. Kublai wins the four-year war, but the western khans no longer fully obey him: the empire splits into the Yuan, the Ilkhanate, the Golden Horde and the Chagatai Khanate.
events.search: Kublai Khan Ariq Böke

events.title: War between the Golden Horde and the Ilkhanate
events.summary: The first open war between Mongol khanates: Berke of the Golden Horde, a convert to Islam, fights Hülegü of the Ilkhanate over the Caucasus and the sack of Baghdad. Berke allies with the Mamluks, and Hülegü's army is defeated on the frozen Terek River in 1263.
events.search: Berke Hülegü

events.title: Siege of Xiangyang
events.place: Xiangyang and Fancheng, on the Han River
events.summary: The Mongols besiege the twin Song cities of Xiangyang and Fancheng for five years. Counterweight trebuchets built by engineers from the Ilkhanate finally break the walls, opening the Yangtze valley to the Mongols.
events.search: Xiangyang siege

events.title: Kublai founds the Yuan dynasty
events.summary: Kublai takes the Chinese dynastic name Yuan and rules from Dadu, his new capital on the site of today's Beijing. The Great Khans are now Chinese emperors as well.
events.search: Yuan dynasty

events.title: First Mongol invasion of Japan
events.summary: A Mongol and Korean fleet lands at Hakata Bay. After a day of fighting the invaders return to their ships, and a storm wrecks much of the fleet on the way home.
events.search: Mongol invasions of Japan

events.title: Marco Polo reaches Kublai's court
events.summary: The Venetian Marco Polo arrives at Shangdu with his father and uncle and stays in Kublai's service for about seventeen years. The book of his travels made the Mongol court famous in Europe.
events.search: Marco Polo

events.title: Battle of Yamen
events.place: Yamen, at the mouth of the Pearl River
events.summary: In a naval battle in the Pearl River delta the Yuan fleet destroys the last Song forces. A Song minister leaps into the sea with the child emperor, ending the Song dynasty; for the first time all of China is under Mongol rule.
events.search: Song dynasty fall Yamen

events.title: Second Mongol invasion of Japan
events.summary: A far larger invasion, with fleets from Korea and southern China, is held off by Japanese coastal walls around Hakata. A typhoon, later called the kamikaze or divine wind, then destroys much of the fleet off Takashima.
events.search: Mongol invasions of Japan kamikaze

events.title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
events.summary: On the Bạch Đằng River, the general Trần Hưng Đạo lures the Yuan fleet onto iron-tipped stakes hidden in the riverbed at low tide. The third Mongol invasion of Đại Việt ends in defeat.
events.search: Tran Hung Dao

events.title: Death of Kublai Khan
events.summary: Kublai dies at Dadu, aged 78, and is succeeded by his grandson Temür. He is the last Great Khan whose authority reached, at least in name, across the whole empire.
events.search: Kublai Khan

events.title: Peace among the khanates
events.place: Agreed between the khans' courts; shown at the Yuan capital, Dadu
events.summary: The khans Temür of the Yuan, Duwa of the Chagatai Khanate, Toqta of the Golden Horde and Öljaitü of the Ilkhanate make peace and recognise the Yuan emperor as their nominal overlord. The truce eases trade and travel along the Silk Road, the period often called the Pax Mongolica.
events.search: Pax Mongolica

events.title: Siege of Caffa and the Black Death
events.summary: The Golden Horde under Jani Beg besieges the Genoese port of Caffa. Plague breaks out among the besiegers, and the notary Gabriele de' Mussi wrote that corpses were thrown over the walls. Ships leaving Caffa are thought to have helped carry the Black Death to Europe.
events.search: Black Death

events.title: The Ming take Dadu
events.summary: Ming armies take Dadu, and the last Yuan emperor, Toghon Temür, flees to the steppe. Mongol rule in China ends, though the Northern Yuan keep the title in Mongolia.
events.search: Ming dynasty founding

events.title: The Louisiana Purchase
events.place: New Orleans, where the territory was handed over
events.summary: The United States buys Louisiana from Napoleon's France for 15 million dollars: about 2.1 million km² between the Mississippi and the Rocky Mountains, which roughly doubles the country. The treaty is signed in Paris on 30 April and the land is handed over at New Orleans in December. Most of it is still the home of Native American nations, whose land the United States takes over in the following decades.
events.search: Louisiana Purchase

events.title: The Russian-American Company
events.place: Sitka, founded that year as the fort of Saint Michael
events.summary: Tsar Paul I gives the Russian-American Company a monopoly over Russian America, the Aleutians and the Alaskan coast, where Russian traders hunt sea otters for their fur. Its fort at Sitka is destroyed by the Tlingit in 1802 and rebuilt as New Archangel, the colony's capital from 1808. Russia rules the land until it sells it to the United States in 1867.
events.search: Russian-American Company

events.title: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
events.place: Guadalupe Hidalgo, just north of Mexico City
events.summary: The treaty ends the Mexican–American War. Mexico gives up about 1.36 million km², its northern lands of Alta California and Nuevo México (today's California, Nevada and Utah, most of Arizona and parts of New Mexico, Colorado and Wyoming), and accepts the Rio Grande as the border of Texas. The United States pays 15 million dollars. With Texas, Mexico has lost about half of its territory since 1836.
events.search: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo

events.title: Canadian Confederation
events.place: Ottawa, the capital of the new Dominion
events.summary: On 1 July the British North America Act unites the Province of Canada, split into Ontario and Quebec, with Nova Scotia and New Brunswick in a federation, the Dominion of Canada. It runs its own affairs while Britain keeps its foreign policy. John A. Macdonald is the first prime minister, and Canadians celebrate the day as Canada Day.
events.search: Canadian Confederation

events.title: Canada takes over Rupert's Land
events.place: Fort Garry, on the Red River (today's Winnipeg)
events.summary: On 15 July the Hudson's Bay Company's Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory pass to Canada, which pays the company 300,000 pounds. After the Red River Resistance led by Louis Riel and the Métis, the Manitoba Act makes Manitoba the fifth province. The rest becomes the North-West Territories, and Canada now reaches from the Atlantic to the Rocky Mountains.
events.search: Rupert's Land transfer

events.title: British Columbia joins Canada
events.summary: On 20 July the colony of British Columbia becomes Canada's sixth province. In return Canada promises a railway to the Pacific within ten years: the Canadian Pacific Railway reaches the coast in 1885. Canada now stretches from ocean to ocean.
events.search: British Columbia joins Confederation 1871

events.title: Prince Edward Island joins Canada
events.place: Charlottetown, where the talks that led to Confederation began in 1864
events.summary: On 1 July the island, which had stayed out in 1867, becomes Canada's seventh province. Deep in debt from building its railway, it joins once Canada agrees to take over the debt and to help buy out the absentee landlords who owned most of its land.
events.search: Prince Edward Island joins Confederation 1873

events.title: Britain hands Canada the Arctic islands
events.summary: On 1 September a British order in council transfers to Canada all of Britain's lands and islands in North America not yet part of it, chiefly the Arctic Archipelago. Most of the islands had been charted by British explorers searching for the Northwest Passage, and the Inuit lived along their coasts.
events.search: Adjacent Territories Order 1880

events.title: Yukon becomes a territory
events.summary: On 13 June, at the height of the Klondike Gold Rush, Canada makes the Yukon a territory of its own, split from the North-West Territories. Tens of thousands of prospectors have poured in, and Dawson City has grown into one of the largest towns in western Canada.
events.search: Yukon Territory Act 1898

events.title: Alberta and Saskatchewan become provinces
events.place: Edmonton and Regina, the new capitals
events.summary: On 1 September Canada carves two provinces out of the North-West Territories, where settlers have flooded onto the prairies along the new railways. Alberta and Saskatchewan become the eighth and ninth provinces, with Edmonton and Regina as their capitals.
events.search: Alberta and Saskatchewan become provinces 1905

events.title: Newfoundland joins Canada
events.summary: On 31 March Newfoundland and Labrador becomes Canada's tenth province. Ruled by a British commission since its debts forced it to give up self-government in 1934, Newfoundland chose to join Canada by 52 percent of the vote in the second of two referendums in 1948.
events.search: Newfoundland joins Confederation 1949

events.title: Nunavut is created
events.summary: On 1 April the eastern half of the Northwest Territories becomes Nunavut, "our land" in Inuktitut, a territory where most people are Inuit. It comes out of the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement of 1993, the largest land claim settled in Canada's history.
events.search: Nunavut 1999

events.title: The Federation of Australia
events.place: Centennial Park, Sydney, where the Commonwealth was proclaimed
events.summary: On 1 January the six British colonies of Australia unite as the Commonwealth of Australia, a self-governing federation under the British Crown. Edmund Barton is the first prime minister. Parliament sits in Melbourne until Canberra, the new capital built for it, opens in 1927.
events.search: Federation of Australia

events.title: New Zealand becomes a dominion
events.summary: On 26 September the colony of New Zealand, self-governing since the 1850s, takes the title of Dominion, on the same footing as Canada and Australia. Britain still answers for its foreign affairs, and New Zealand only takes up full independence in law in 1947.
events.search: Dominion of New Zealand 1907

events.title: Newfoundland becomes a dominion
events.summary: On 26 September Newfoundland, with Labrador, self-governing since 1855, becomes a dominion of the British Empire, like New Zealand the same day. Crushing debts in the Great Depression lead it to hand its government to a British commission in 1934, until it joins Canada in 1949.
events.search: Dominion of Newfoundland

events.title: The Union of South Africa
events.place: Cape Town, where the new parliament sits
events.summary: On 31 May, eight years after the Boer War, the Cape, Natal, the Transvaal and the Orange River Colony unite as the Union of South Africa, a self-governing dominion with Louis Botha as prime minister. Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein share the role of capital. Black South Africans are kept almost entirely out of its politics. From 1920 it also rules South West Africa, today's Namibia, under a League of Nations mandate.
events.search: Union of South Africa 1910

events.title: Denmark claims all of Greenland
events.summary: Denmark, whose colonies lay along Greenland's west and south coasts, declares its sovereignty over the whole island. Norway contests it and occupies part of the east coast in 1931, but in 1933 the Permanent Court of International Justice rules for Denmark.
events.search: Danish sovereignty over Greenland 1921

events.title: The Armistice of 11 November
events.place: Marshal Foch's railway carriage in the forest of Compiègne, near Rethondes
events.summary: At dawn on 11 November, in Marshal Foch's railway carriage in the forest of Compiègne, German envoys sign the armistice with the Allies. The guns fall silent at 11 o'clock, after four years of war and some 17 million dead. Germany must leave the lands it occupies, Alsace and Lorraine included, hand over its heavy weapons and fleet and let the Allies occupy the left bank of the Rhine. Peace itself comes with the Treaty of Versailles in 1919. In June 1940 Hitler had France sign its own armistice in the same carriage.
events.search: Armistice 11 November 1918

events.title: Germany surrenders on 8 May
events.place: Berlin-Karlshorst, after a first signing in Reims
events.summary: A week after Hitler's suicide, Germany surrenders without conditions. General Jodl signs a first act in Reims on 7 May, at Eisenhower's headquarters; at Stalin's demand a second is signed in Berlin-Karlshorst late on 8 May by Marshal Keitel, before Marshal Zhukov and the Western Allies, with General de Lattre de Tassigny for France. The fighting stops at 23:01 that night, already 9 May in Moscow, which is why Russia marks Victory Day a day later. This was a surrender, not an armistice: Germany was occupied and divided by the four Allies. The war went on against Japan until September.
events.search: German surrender 1945 V-E Day

events.title: Brazil declares its independence, 7 September 1822
events.summary: Prince Pedro, left behind in Brazil as regent, refuses to return to Lisbon and declares Brazil independent on the banks of the Ipiranga. Crowned Emperor Pedro I in December, he wins a short war against Portuguese garrisons; Portugal recognises the Empire of Brazil in 1825.
events.search: Independence of Brazil Ipiranga

events.title: The Liberal Wars end at Évoramonte, 26 May 1834
events.summary: In 1828 Dom Miguel seized the throne from his niece Maria II and ruled as an absolute king. Her father Pedro, the former Emperor of Brazil, landed near Porto with a liberal army in 1832; after two years of civil war Miguel surrenders at Évoramonte and leaves for exile, and Maria II reigns as a constitutional queen.
events.search: Liberal Wars Concession of Evoramonte

events.title: Portugal founds Moçâmedes, 1840
events.summary: A Portuguese expedition from Luanda builds a fort and trading posts on the bay of Moçâmedes, far south of Benguela, after a pact with the local Herero chiefs. Settlers from Madeira and Brazil follow, and the town becomes the base of Portugal's push into the south of Angola.
events.search: Moçâmedes Namibe founded

events.title: President Grant awards Bolama to Portugal, 21 April 1870
events.summary: Britain and Portugal had both claimed the island of Bolama, off the coast of Guinea, since the 1790s. Asked to arbitrate, United States President Ulysses S. Grant rules for Portugal; Bolama becomes the capital of Portuguese Guinea when it is separated from Cape Verde in 1879.
events.search: Bolama arbitration Grant

events.title: MacMahon's award gives Delagoa Bay to Portugal, 1875
events.summary: Britain claimed the southern shore of Delagoa Bay and its islands, the best harbour between Natal and Mozambique. The French president, Marshal MacMahon, arbitrates and gives the whole bay to Portugal; Lourenço Marques grows into the port of the Transvaal and later the capital of Mozambique.
events.search: Delagoa Bay arbitration MacMahon

events.title: Treaty of Simulambuco, 1 February 1885
events.summary: While the Berlin Conference divides Africa, the princes and chiefs of Cabinda sign a treaty placing their land under Portuguese protection. It gives Portugal the coast north of the Congo, which a strip handed to the Congo Free State soon cuts off from the rest of Angola.
events.search: Treaty of Simulambuco Cabinda

events.title: The British Ultimatum, 11 January 1890
events.summary: Portugal's Pink Map claimed all the land between Angola and Mozambique, across Britain's route from the Cape to Cairo. Britain orders Portuguese troops out of the Shire highlands and Mashonaland under threat of war, and Lisbon gives in. The humiliation feeds the republican movement that overthrows the monarchy twenty years later.
events.search: British Ultimatum 1890 Pink Map

events.title: The Anglo-Portuguese Treaty, 11 June 1891
events.summary: Signed in London after the Ultimatum, the treaty fixes the borders of Angola and Mozambique with British Central Africa and Rhodesia. Portugal keeps the interior of Mozambique, including Manica, but gives up the land between its two colonies.
events.search: Anglo-Portuguese Treaty 1891

events.title: King Carlos is killed in Lisbon, 1 February 1908
events.summary: Republican gunmen shoot King Carlos I and his heir Luís Filipe as the royal carriage crosses the Terreiro do Paço. The young Manuel II takes the throne, but the monarchy never recovers and falls two years later.
events.search: Lisbon Regicide King Carlos

events.title: Portugal becomes a republic, 5 October 1910
events.summary: After two days of fighting in Lisbon, the republic is proclaimed from the balcony of the City Hall. King Manuel II sails into exile in England, ending almost eight centuries of monarchy.
events.search: 5 October 1910 revolution Portuguese Republic

events.title: Portugal enters the First World War, 9 March 1916
events.summary: At Britain's request Portugal seizes the German ships in its harbours, and Germany declares war. Portugal was already fighting the Germans on the borders of Angola and Mozambique. It sends an expeditionary corps to Flanders, which is broken at the Battle of La Lys in April 1918.
events.search: Portugal First World War 1916

events.title: The 28 May coup ends the First Republic, 1926
events.summary: General Gomes da Costa marches on Lisbon from Braga and the army takes power without a fight. Sixteen years of unstable republic, with dozens of governments, give way to a military dictatorship, the Ditadura Nacional.
events.search: 28 May 1926 coup Portugal

events.title: Salazar's Estado Novo constitution, 11 April 1933
events.summary: A new constitution, approved in a plebiscite, founds the Estado Novo. António de Oliveira Salazar, prime minister since 1932, rules a single-party, corporatist state with censorship and a political police, the PVDE, later PIDE. The regime lasts 41 years.
events.search: Estado Novo constitution 1933 Salazar

events.title: Japan invades Portuguese Timor, 20 February 1942
events.summary: Japanese troops land at Dili, although Portugal is neutral. Australian and Dutch commandos, helped by Timorese, fight on in the mountains for a year. The occupation lasts until Japan's surrender in 1945, and tens of thousands of Timorese die.
events.search: Battle of Timor Japanese invasion 1942

events.title: Volunteers seize Dadra and Nagar Haveli, 2 August 1954
events.summary: Indian volunteers take Dadra and then Nagar Haveli, two Portuguese enclaves cut off from the coast. India blocks Portuguese troops from crossing its land, and the enclaves govern themselves as Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli until India annexes them in 1961.
events.search: Dadra and Nagar Haveli 1954 liberation

events.title: General Delgado challenges the regime, 1958
events.summary: Humberto Delgado runs for president against the Estado Novo's candidate and promises to dismiss Salazar. Huge crowds greet him in Porto and Lisbon, but the vote of 8 June is rigged and he is credited with only a quarter of it. He goes into exile and is murdered by the PIDE in 1965.
events.search: Humberto Delgado 1958 election

events.title: The colonial war begins in Angola, 4 February 1961
events.summary: Nationalists attack Luanda's prisons, and in March a large uprising breaks out in the north. The war spreads to Guinea in 1963 and Mozambique in 1964. For thirteen years Portugal fights on three fronts, until the army itself overthrows the regime in 1974.
events.search: Portuguese Colonial War Angola 1961

events.title: India takes Goa, Daman and Diu, 19 December 1961
events.summary: After years of failed talks, the Indian army moves into Portugal's last enclaves in India. Salazar orders a fight to the death, but Governor Vassalo e Silva surrenders after 36 hours. Portugal recognises the loss only after the Carnation Revolution, in 1974.
events.search: Indian annexation of Goa 1961

events.title: Caetano replaces Salazar, 27 September 1968
events.summary: After a stroke leaves Salazar unable to rule, Marcello Caetano takes over as head of government. His promise of a cautious opening, the 'Marcelist spring', soon fades, and the colonial wars go on. Salazar dies in 1970, still believing he was in charge.
events.search: Marcello Caetano Salazar 1968

events.title: The Carnation Revolution, 25 April 1974
events.summary: Young officers of the Armed Forces Movement overthrow the Estado Novo dictatorship in an almost bloodless coup. Crowds fill the streets of Lisbon and put carnations in the soldiers' rifles. The revolution opens the way to democracy and to the end of the colonial wars in Africa.
events.search: Carnation Revolution

events.title: Portugal recognises Guinea-Bissau, 10 September 1974
events.summary: After eleven years of war against the PAIGC, Portugal recognises the independence Guinea-Bissau had declared in 1973. It is the first of Portugal's African colonies to become independent.
events.search: Guinea-Bissau

events.title: Independence of Mozambique, 25 June 1975
events.summary: Mozambique becomes independent under FRELIMO, which had fought Portuguese rule since 1964. Samora Machel is its first president.
events.search: Mozambique

events.title: Independence of Cape Verde, 5 July 1975
events.summary: The islands of Cape Verde become independent, led by the PAIGC, the party that also freed Guinea-Bissau.
events.search: Cape Verde

events.title: Independence of São Tomé and Príncipe, 12 July 1975
events.summary: The islands of São Tomé and Príncipe, in the Gulf of Guinea, become independent, with Manuel Pinto da Costa as their first president.
events.search: São Tomé and Príncipe

events.title: Independence of Angola, 11 November 1975
events.summary: Portugal leaves Angola as its three liberation movements fight for power. The MPLA proclaims independence in Luanda, and the civil war that follows lasts until 2002. Hundreds of thousands of Portuguese settlers return to Portugal.
events.search: Angola

events.title: The 25 November 1975 coup attempt
events.summary: Radical left-wing military units try to take power and are stopped by moderate officers. The failed coup ends the revolutionary period that followed 1974 and sets Portugal on the path to a parliamentary democracy.
events.search: Coup of 25 November 1975

events.title: Indonesia invades East Timor, 7 December 1975
events.summary: Nine days after East Timor declared its independence from Portugal, Indonesia invades it and annexes it the next year. The United Nations never recognises the annexation and goes on listing the land as a territory under Portuguese administration, until the Timorese vote for independence in 1999.
events.search: Indonesian invasion of East Timor

events.title: The Constitution of 2 April 1976
events.place: Assembly of the Republic, São Bento Palace, Lisbon
events.summary: The Constituent Assembly elected in 1975 adopts the Constitution that still governs Portugal. It founds the democratic republic and makes the Azores and Madeira autonomous regions, each with its own government and assembly.
events.search: Constitution of Portugal

events.title: Prime Minister Sá Carneiro dies, 4 December 1980
events.summary: Francisco Sá Carneiro, prime minister for less than a year, is killed with his defence minister when their small plane crashes just after take-off, three days before the presidential election. Whether it was an accident or an attack is still debated.
events.search: 1980 Camarate air crash

events.title: Portugal joins the European Community, 1 January 1986
events.place: Jerónimos Monastery, Lisbon, where the treaty was signed
events.summary: Portugal and Spain join the European Economic Community. The accession treaty was signed at the Jerónimos Monastery in June 1985. European funds help transform the country's roads, schools and economy in the years that follow.
events.search: 1986 enlargement of the European Communities

events.title: Expo 98, the Lisbon World's Fair
events.summary: From May to September, Lisbon hosts a World's Fair on the theme of the oceans, five hundred years after Vasco da Gama reached India. Some eleven million visits are made, and the old industrial riverside becomes a new district, the Parque das Nações, with the Vasco da Gama Bridge.
events.search: Expo 98

events.title: Macau is handed over to China, 20 December 1999
events.summary: At midnight Portugal hands Macau back to China, as agreed in 1987, ending more than four centuries of Portuguese presence. Macau becomes a special administrative region that keeps its own laws and system for fifty years. It is the last of Portugal's overseas territories.
events.search: Transfer of sovereignty over Macau

events.title: The euro replaces the escudo, 1 January 2002
events.summary: Euro notes and coins come into use and the escudo, Portugal's currency since 1911, is withdrawn two months later. The euro had been Portugal's currency on paper since 1999.
events.search: Portuguese euro coins

events.title: The Treaty of Lisbon, 13 December 2007
events.summary: The leaders of the European Union sign the treaty that reforms how the Union works, during Portugal's presidency. It comes into force in December 2009.
events.search: Treaty of Lisbon

events.title: The EU and IMF bailout, May 2011
events.summary: Unable to borrow on the markets, Portugal receives a 78-billion-euro rescue from the European Union and the International Monetary Fund. Three years of austerity follow, and Portugal leaves the programme in 2014.
events.search: 2010–2014 Portuguese financial crisis

events.title: The generals' putsch in Algiers, 21–26 April 1961
events.summary: Four retired generals, Challe, Jouhaud, Salan and Zeller, seize Algiers with paratroopers to stop de Gaulle from giving Algeria its independence. De Gaulle takes emergency powers and calls on soldiers and citizens by radio and television to refuse to follow them. Conscripts stay loyal and the putsch collapses in four days.
events.search: Algiers putsch 1961

events.title: Algeria becomes independent, 5 July 1962
events.summary: The Évian Accords of 18 March 1962 end almost eight years of war between France and the Algerian National Liberation Front. On 1 July Algerians vote for independence by an overwhelming majority, and Algeria becomes independent on 5 July, 132 years after the French landing of 1830. Nearly a million European settlers, the pieds-noirs, and tens of thousands of harkis leave for France.
events.search: Évian Accords Algerian independence

events.title: The Élysée Treaty, 22 January 1963
events.summary: Charles de Gaulle and Konrad Adenauer sign a treaty of friendship between France and West Germany, enemies in three wars in seventy years. Their governments agree to meet regularly and to consult each other on foreign policy, and a youth office brings millions of young French and Germans together in the decades that follow.
events.search: Élysée Treaty

events.title: France leaves NATO's integrated command, 1966
events.summary: In a letter to President Johnson on 7 March 1966, de Gaulle announces that France is leaving NATO's integrated military command while staying in the Alliance. Allied troops and bases leave French soil, and NATO's headquarters move from near Paris to Belgium in 1967. France returns to the integrated command in 2009.
events.search: France NATO 1966

events.title: First nuclear test at Moruroa, 2 July 1966
events.summary: Having left the Algerian Sahara, France sets off its first nuclear bomb in the Pacific over the atoll of Moruroa. Some 190 tests follow at Moruroa and Fangataufa, in the air until 1974 and then underground. The last series, in 1995–1996, sets off protests around the world before France stops testing for good.
events.search: Moruroa nuclear test

events.title: May 68
events.summary: Student protests in Nanterre and at the Sorbonne turn into street battles in the Latin Quarter, then into the largest general strike in French history, with some ten million workers out. De Gaulle dissolves the National Assembly on 30 May and his supporters win the June elections, but the crisis changes French society, from universities to the workplace.
events.search: May 68

events.title: De Gaulle resigns, 28 April 1969
events.summary: De Gaulle had staked his office on a referendum to create regions and reform the Senate. When 52 per cent vote no on 27 April, he resigns the next day and retires to Colombey-les-Deux-Églises, where he dies the following year. Georges Pompidou is elected president in June.
events.search: de Gaulle resigns 1969 referendum

events.title: The Comoros declare independence, 6 July 1975
events.summary: In a referendum in December 1974, Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli vote for independence, but Mayotte votes to stay French. When France insists on counting the islands one by one, the Comorian parliament declares the whole archipelago independent. Mayotte stays French after another vote in 1976, and the Comoros still claim it.
events.search: Comoros independence Mayotte

events.title: Djibouti becomes independent, 27 June 1977
events.summary: After a referendum in May in which almost all voters choose independence, the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas becomes the Republic of Djibouti, with Hassan Gouled Aptidon as its first president. It is the last French colony in Africa to become independent. France keeps a large military base there.
events.search: Djibouti independence 1977

events.title: The New Hebrides become Vanuatu, 30 July 1980
events.summary: Ruled jointly by France and Britain since 1906, with two of everything from police to schools, the New Hebrides become independent as Vanuatu under Prime Minister Walter Lini. A French-speaking rebellion on Espiritu Santo, the Coconut War, is put down within weeks with the help of troops from Papua New Guinea.
events.search: Vanuatu independence New Hebrides

events.title: France abolishes the death penalty, 9 October 1981
events.summary: Months after François Mitterrand's election, Justice Minister Robert Badinter carries the law abolishing the death penalty through Parliament, against the majority of public opinion. The guillotine, last used in 1977, is retired. Abolition was written into the Constitution in 2007.
events.search: death penalty abolished France 1981

events.title: The Ouvéa crisis and the Matignon Accords, 1988
events.summary: After years of violence between Kanak independence fighters and loyalists, militants take gendarmes hostage in a cave on Ouvéa in April 1988. The army's assault on 5 May leaves nineteen Kanaks and two soldiers dead. Shocked, the two sides sign the Matignon Accords on 26 June with Prime Minister Michel Rocard, promising development and a vote on independence in ten years.
events.search: Matignon Accords Ouvéa 1988

events.title: The Channel Tunnel opens, 6 May 1994
events.summary: Queen Elizabeth II and President Mitterrand open the tunnel under the Channel between Coquelles and Folkestone, 50 kilometres long, 38 of them under the sea. For the first time since the Ice Age, Britain is joined to the Continent by land, and trains link London to Paris and Brussels in about three hours.
events.search: Channel Tunnel

events.title: The Nouméa Accord, 5 May 1998
events.summary: Ten years after Matignon, the State, the independence movement and the loyalists agree on a path for New Caledonia: powers handed over step by step, a New Caledonian citizenship, recognition of Kanak identity, and up to three referendums on independence. The Constitution is amended to make room for this unique status.
events.search: Nouméa Accord

events.title: The euro replaces the franc, 1 January 2002
events.summary: Euro notes and coins come into use, and the franc, France's currency since 1795, is withdrawn on 17 February. The euro had been France's currency on paper since 1999.
events.search: French euro coins

events.title: Saint Martin and Saint Barthélemy leave Guadeloupe, 15 July 2007
events.summary: After voting for it in 2003, the two small islands, governed from Guadeloupe until then, become overseas collectivities of France, each with its own elected council. Saint Martin shares its island with Sint Maarten, a part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
events.search: Saint Martin Saint Barthélemy collectivity 2007

events.title: Mayotte becomes the 101st department, 31 March 2011
events.summary: After a referendum in 2009 in which 95 per cent voted yes, Mayotte becomes an overseas department of France, and in 2014 a part of the European Union. The Comoros, which have claimed the island since 1975, protest.
events.search: Mayotte department 2011

events.title: New Caledonia votes on independence, 2018–2021
events.summary: As the Nouméa Accord provided, New Caledonians vote three times on independence. No wins with 57 per cent in 2018 and 53 per cent in 2020. The third vote, in December 2021, held during the COVID-19 epidemic, is boycotted by the independence parties and gives 96 per cent no. The territory's future status is still under negotiation.
events.search: New Caledonia independence referendum

events.title: The Treaty of Rome, 25 March 1957
events.summary: France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg sign the treaties that found the European Economic Community and Euratom. They come into force on 1 January 1958 and open a common market that grows into today's European Union.
events.search: Treaty of Rome EEC

events.title: The Battle of Algiers, 1957
events.summary: Given police powers in Algiers in January 1957, General Massu's paratroopers break the National Liberation Front's bombing network in the Casbah by October. They win through mass arrests and the systematic use of torture, which, once revealed, turns much of French opinion against the war.
events.search: Battle of Algiers 1957

events.title: The 13 May 1958 crisis and de Gaulle's return
events.summary: Settlers and army officers seize the Government General in Algiers and set up a Committee of Public Safety under General Massu, calling for Charles de Gaulle. Paratroopers take Corsica and a landing on Paris is planned. To avoid civil war, the National Assembly makes de Gaulle head of government on 1 June, with powers to write a new constitution.
events.search: May 1958 crisis

events.title: The Fifth Republic's constitution, 4 October 1958
events.summary: Approved by four out of five voters in the referendum of 28 September, the new constitution gives a strong president the upper hand over Parliament and creates the French Community for the colonies. It is promulgated on 4 October, and de Gaulle is elected the first president of the Fifth Republic in December.
events.search: Fifth Republic constitution 1958

events.title: Guinea says no and becomes independent, 2 October 1958
events.summary: "We prefer poverty in freedom to riches in slavery," Sékou Touré tells de Gaulle in Conakry in August. In the referendum of 28 September, 95 per cent of Guineans reject the French Community, the only colony to do so, and Guinea declares its independence four days later. France withdraws its officials and aid at once.
events.search: Guinea independence 1958

events.title: Barricades Week in Algiers, 24 January – 1 February 1960
events.summary: Angered by de Gaulle's offer of self-determination to Algeria and the recall of General Massu, settler activists raise barricades in the centre of Algiers. On the first day, shooting kills 14 gendarmes and 8 demonstrators. After de Gaulle appeals on television to the army's loyalty, the insurgents surrender a week later.
events.search: Barricades Week Algiers 1960

events.title: Gerboise bleue, France's first atomic bomb, 13 February 1960
events.summary: France sets off a 70-kiloton atomic bomb on a tower in the desert near Reggane and becomes the world's fourth nuclear power. Sixteen more tests follow in the Algerian Sahara until 1966, at Reggane and then underground at In Ekker, under a clause of the Évian Accords, before testing moves to French Polynesia.
events.search: Gerboise Bleue nuclear test

events.title: The Year of Africa, 1960
events.place: French West and Equatorial Africa, Cameroon, Togo and Madagascar
events.summary: Fourteen of France's African colonies and trust territories become independent in a single year, from Cameroon in January to Mauritania in November, most of them peacefully and by agreement. Most sign cooperation and defence agreements with France and keep the CFA franc, ties that last for decades.
events.search: Year of Africa 1960

events.title: The Mali Federation splits, 20 August 1960
events.summary: Two months after independence, Senegal and the Sudanese Republic fall out over who should lead their federation. In the night of 19–20 August, Senegal withdraws and sends Modibo Keïta and his ministers back to Bamako by sealed train. Léopold Sédar Senghor becomes president of Senegal, and the Sudanese Republic takes the name Mali on 22 September.
events.search: Mali Federation breakup

events.title: The Paris massacre, 17 October 1961
events.summary: Tens of thousands of Algerians march peacefully in Paris against a curfew imposed on them alone. The police of prefect Maurice Papon charge them; some 11,000 are arrested and dozens, perhaps more than a hundred, are killed, some thrown into the Seine. Long denied, the massacre was acknowledged by the French state in 2012.
events.search: Paris massacre 17 October 1961

events.title: The Fourth Republic and the French Union, 27 October 1946
events.summary: After a first draft was rejected in May, a second constitution is approved by referendum on 13 October and promulgated on 27 October 1946. It founds the Fourth Republic, a parliamentary regime, and replaces the colonial empire with the French Union: the colonies become overseas territories and departments, and their peoples become citizens.
events.search: French Fourth Republic constitution 1946

events.title: Tende and La Brigue become French, 1947
events.summary: The peace treaty signed with Italy in Paris on 10 February 1947 moves the border in the Alps: Tende and La Brigue, in the upper Roya valley, and a few mountain passes pass to France. A local referendum confirms the change in October 1947, a month after the treaty comes into force on 15 September.
events.search: Paris Peace Treaty 1947 Tende La Brigue

events.title: The Malagasy Uprising, 29 March 1947
events.summary: Nationalist insurgents attack French posts and plantations in eastern Madagascar, starting at Moramanga. The revolt spreads over a third of the island before French troops crush it by 1948. Tens of thousands of Malagasy die in the fighting, the reprisals and the famine that follows, and the island's deputies are tried and condemned.
events.search: Malagasy Uprising 1947

events.title: The European Coal and Steel Community, 18 April 1951
events.summary: A year after Robert Schuman's declaration of 9 May 1950, France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg sign in Paris the treaty that puts their coal and steel under a common High Authority. Meant to make another war between France and Germany impossible, it is the first step towards the European Union.
events.search: Treaty of Paris 1951 European Coal and Steel Community

events.title: The Toussaint Rouge starts the Algerian War, 1 November 1954
events.summary: In the night of All Saints' Day, the newly founded National Liberation Front sets off some thirty attacks across Algeria, most of them in the Aurès, and calls for independence. The French government answers that Algeria is France. It is the start of an eight-year war that ends with Algeria's independence in 1962.
events.search: Toussaint Rouge 1 November 1954 Algerian War

events.title: Morocco becomes independent, 2 March 1956
events.summary: Sultan Mohammed V, deposed and exiled by France in 1953, returns in triumph in November 1955. On 2 March 1956 France ends its protectorate; Spain gives up its northern zone on 7 April, and the Tangier International Zone joins Morocco in October. Spain keeps Cape Juby until 1958 and Ifni until 1969.
events.search: Morocco independence 1956

events.title: Tunisia becomes independent, 20 March 1956
events.summary: After years of armed resistance and negotiations led by Habib Bourguiba, internal autonomy in 1955 is followed by full independence on 20 March 1956, under the Bey. On 25 July 1957 the Constituent Assembly abolishes the monarchy and makes Bourguiba president of the Republic.
events.search: Tunisia independence 1956

events.title: The Indochina War begins, 19 December 1946
events.summary: Talks between France and Ho Chi Minh's Democratic Republic of Vietnam, proclaimed in September 1945, break down. After the French navy shells Haiphong in November, the Viet Minh attack the French in Hanoi on 19 December 1946. The war lasts nearly eight years and ends with the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu.
events.search: First Indochina War 1946 Haiphong Hanoi

events.title: Laos becomes independent, 22 October 1953
events.summary: A kingdom under French protection since 1947, Laos gains full sovereignty by the Franco-Lao Treaty of Amity and Association, signed in Paris on 22 October 1953, while Viet Minh troops and the Pathet Lao hold the north-east. The Geneva Accords confirm its independence the next year.
events.search: Laos independence 1953 Franco-Lao treaty

events.title: Cambodia becomes independent, 9 November 1953
events.summary: King Norodom Sihanouk's "royal crusade for independence" takes him to France, the United States and into self-imposed exile. France gives way and hands over the army, the police and the courts; the last French troops leave and Cambodia celebrates its independence on 9 November 1953.
events.search: Cambodia independence 9 November 1953 Sihanouk

events.title: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu, 13 March – 7 May 1954
events.summary: The French army builds an entrenched camp in a remote valley of north-west Tonkin to draw the Viet Minh into a pitched battle. General Võ Nguyên Giáp surrounds it with artillery hauled over the mountains, and after 56 days of siege the camp falls on 7 May 1954. The defeat brings France to accept peace at Geneva.
events.search: Battle of Dien Bien Phu 1954

events.title: The Geneva Accords divide Vietnam, 21 July 1954
events.place: Bến Hải river, Vietnam (signed in Geneva)
events.summary: The conference in Geneva ends the Indochina War. Vietnam is split at the Bến Hải river, near the 17th parallel: the Viet Minh's Democratic Republic of Vietnam in the north, the State of Vietnam in the south, until elections promised for 1956 that are never held. The independence of Laos and Cambodia is confirmed, and French troops leave.
events.search: Geneva Accords 1954 Indochina 17th parallel

events.title: French India passes to India, 1 November 1954
events.summary: After Chandernagore joined India in 1950, the councillors of Pondichéry, Karikal, Mahé and Yanaon vote in October 1954 to join India too. France hands over their administration on 1 November 1954; the treaty of cession, signed in 1956, is ratified by France only in 1962. The four towns form today's Puducherry.
events.search: French India transfer to India 1954 Pondicherry

events.title: The Saar rejects the Saar Statute, 23 October 1955
events.summary: France and West Germany agree to give the Saar, a French protectorate since 1947, a European status under the Western European Union. In a referendum on 23 October 1955, two thirds of the Saarlanders vote no. France accepts the result, and the Saar joins West Germany on 1 January 1957.
events.search: Saar Statute referendum 1955

events.title: Operation Passage to Freedom, August 1954 – May 1955
events.summary: The Geneva Accords give people 300 days to choose between North and South. French and American ships carry between 800,000 and a million people from Haiphong to the South, most of them Catholics, while tens of thousands of Viet Minh fighters and their families go north. The North is left to the Viet Minh, and the South gains a large community loyal to its government.
events.search: Operation Passage to Freedom 1954 1955 refugees Haiphong Saigon

events.title: The Republic of Vietnam is proclaimed, 26 October 1955
events.summary: Prime Minister Ngô Đình Diệm calls a referendum against the head of state, the former emperor Bảo Đại, who lives in France. The vote of 23 October 1955 is openly rigged and gives Diệm 98% of the vote. Three days later he proclaims the Republic of Vietnam and becomes its first president; he refuses the elections on reunification promised for 1956.
events.search: Republic of Vietnam proclaimed 1955 Ngo Dinh Diem Bao Dai referendum

events.title: The Vietnam War, 1955 – 1975
events.place: North and South Vietnam, with Laos and Cambodia
events.summary: Communist North Vietnam and the Viet Cong fight to bring down South Vietnam and reunify the country. The United States sends advisers, then from 1965 more than half a million soldiers and a massive bombing campaign; the war spills into Laos and Cambodia along the Ho Chi Minh trail. Some three million people die before the North takes Saigon on 30 April 1975.
events.search: Vietnam War 1955 1975 Second Indochina War American War

events.title: The National Liberation Front (Viet Cong) is founded, 20 December 1960
events.summary: With the backing of Hanoi, communists and other opponents of Ngô Đình Diệm found the National Liberation Front of South Vietnam in a jungle village near the Cambodian border. Its guerrillas, called the Viet Cong by Saigon, take control of large parts of the countryside in the following years.
events.search: National Liberation Front Viet Cong founded 1960

events.title: The coup against Ngô Đình Diệm, 1–2 November 1963
events.summary: After months of Buddhist protests, crushed by force, South Vietnamese generals overthrow President Ngô Đình Diệm with the tacit approval of the United States. Diệm and his brother Ngô Đình Nhu are killed on 2 November 1963. A string of military governments follows, and the South stays unstable for years.
events.search: Coup against Ngo Dinh Diem 1963 Saigon

events.title: The Gulf of Tonkin incident, 2–4 August 1964
events.place: Gulf of Tonkin, off Thanh Hóa
events.summary: North Vietnamese torpedo boats attack the American destroyer USS Maddox on 2 August 1964; a second attack reported two days later most likely never happened. The US Congress passes the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, which lets President Johnson wage war in Vietnam without declaring it, and American planes bomb the North for the first time.
events.search: Gulf of Tonkin incident 1964 resolution USS Maddox

events.title: US combat troops land at Da Nang, 8 March 1965
events.summary: Some 3,500 US Marines come ashore at Da Nang to guard its air base, the first American combat troops in Vietnam. Until then the United States had sent only advisers; by the end of 1965 it has nearly 185,000 soldiers in the South, and more than 500,000 in 1968.
events.search: US Marines land Da Nang 1965 combat troops

events.title: The Tet Offensive, 30 January 1968
events.place: Huế and towns across South Vietnam
events.summary: During the Tết new year truce, the Viet Cong and the North Vietnamese army attack more than a hundred towns of the South at once, even the US embassy in Saigon. They are pushed back with heavy losses, but the battle for Huế lasts a month and leaves the old imperial city in ruins. The shock turns American opinion against the war, and Washington begins to look for a way out.
events.search: Tet Offensive 1968 Battle of Hue

events.title: The Paris Peace Accords, 27 January 1973
events.summary: After four years of talks in Paris, North Vietnam, South Vietnam, the Viet Cong and the United States sign a ceasefire. The last American troops leave South Vietnam on 29 March 1973 and American prisoners are freed, but North Vietnamese troops stay in the South and the fighting soon starts again.
events.search: Paris Peace Accords 1973 Vietnam ceasefire US withdrawal

events.title: The Fall of Saigon, 30 April 1975
events.summary: North Vietnam's spring offensive sweeps through the South in under two months. As its tanks close in, American helicopters lift the last Americans and thousands of South Vietnamese from the roofs of Saigon. On 30 April 1975 a tank breaks through the gate of the presidential palace and South Vietnam surrenders. Saigon is renamed Ho Chi Minh City the next year.
events.search: Fall of Saigon 30 April 1975

events.title: Vietnam is reunified, 2 July 1976
events.summary: Fourteen months after the fall of Saigon, North and South become one country again: the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, with Hanoi as its capital. Saigon is renamed Ho Chi Minh City. Hundreds of thousands of South Vietnamese are sent to re-education camps, and many flee by sea in the following years.
events.search: Vietnam reunification 2 July 1976 Socialist Republic of Vietnam

events.title: France declares war on Germany, 3 September 1939
events.summary: Two days after Germany invades Poland, France and the United Kingdom, bound to Poland by their guarantees, declare war on Germany. Apart from a short offensive in the Saar, the French army waits behind the Maginot Line: months of "phoney war" follow.
events.search: France declares war on Germany 1939 Second World War

events.title: The Battle of France, 10 May – 25 June 1940
events.summary: Germany attacks the Netherlands, Belgium and France. Its tanks cross the Ardennes and break through at Sedan on 13 May, then race to the Channel and trap the Allied armies in the north; more than 300,000 soldiers are evacuated from Dunkirk. Paris falls on 14 June, and in six weeks the French army is beaten.
events.search: Battle of France 1940 Sedan Dunkirk

events.title: The Appeal of 18 June 1940
events.place: Broadcast from London; heard in Brittany and Île de Sein
events.summary: The day after Marshal Pétain asks for an armistice, General Charles de Gaulle speaks on the BBC from London: "Whatever happens, the flame of French resistance must not and shall not go out." Few hear it, but it founds Free France. Among the first to answer are the fishermen of the Île de Sein, who sail to England.
events.search: Appeal of 18 June de Gaulle BBC Free France

events.title: The Armistice of 22 June 1940 divides France
events.summary: Hitler has the armistice signed in the same railway carriage as the German defeat of 1918. Germany occupies the north and the Atlantic coast, three fifths of the country, behind a demarcation line; the south stays a "free zone" under the French government. France keeps its empire and its fleet, and pays the costs of the occupation.
events.search: Armistice of 22 June 1940 Compiègne Rethondes demarcation line

events.title: Pétain is given full powers: Vichy France, 10 July 1940
events.summary: Meeting in the spa town of Vichy, the National Assembly gives Marshal Philippe Pétain full powers to write a new constitution. The next day he makes himself head of the "French State": the Third Republic ends, and the Vichy regime, authoritarian and soon collaborating with Germany, governs France until 1944.
events.search: Vichy France Pétain full powers 10 July 1940 French State

events.title: Japan enters Tonkin, 22 September 1940
events.summary: To cut the supply route to China, Japan forces the French authorities in Indochina to let it station troops in Tonkin. Japanese troops attack the border post of Lạng Sơn the same day before the fighting stops. In July 1941 they spread to all of Indochina, which the French still govern under Japan's watch.
events.search: Japanese invasion of French Indochina 1940 Lang Son

events.title: The Franco-Thai War and the Treaty of Tokyo, 1940 – 1941
events.summary: Thailand seizes on France's defeat to claim the lands it lost in 1904 and 1907. After border fights, its army enters Laos and Cambodia in January 1941; the French navy wins at Koh Chang, but Japan imposes a ceasefire. By the Treaty of Tokyo of 9 May 1941, France cedes Battambang, most of Siem Reap and the land west of the Mekong. Thailand gives them back in 1946.
events.search: Franco-Thai War 1940 1941 Treaty of Tokyo Battambang

events.title: The Syria–Lebanon campaign, 8 June – 14 July 1941
events.summary: Vichy France lets German planes refuel in Syria to help a revolt in Iraq. British, Australian, Indian and Free French troops invade the mandate, and French fight French; Damascus falls on 21 June. By the armistice of Saint-Jean-d'Acre, Syria and Lebanon pass to the Free French, who promise them independence.
events.search: Syria Lebanon campaign 1941 Vichy Free French

events.title: The Battle of Madagascar, 5 May – 6 November 1942
events.summary: Fearing that Vichy France would let Japanese submarines use the naval base of Diego-Suarez, British forces land in the north of Madagascar. After a long campaign across the island, the Vichy governor surrenders in November. The British hand Madagascar over to the Free French in January 1943.
events.search: Battle of Madagascar 1942 Diego-Suarez Operation Ironclad

events.title: Operation Torch: the Allies land in North Africa, 8 November 1942
events.summary: American and British troops land in Morocco and Algeria. Vichy's forces fight for a few days, then Admiral Darlan, in Algiers, orders a ceasefire and French North Africa joins the Allies. The French army of Africa returns to the war, in Tunisia, then in Italy and France.
events.search: Operation Torch 1942 Allied landings North Africa Algiers Casablanca Oran

events.title: Germany and Italy occupy the free zone, 11 November 1942
events.summary: In answer to the Allied landings in North Africa, German troops cross the demarcation line and occupy the south of France, while Italy takes the land east of the Rhône and Corsica. The Vichy government stays in place, but all of France is now occupied.
events.search: Case Anton occupation of the free zone November 1942

events.title: The scuttling of the French fleet at Toulon, 27 November 1942
events.summary: As German troops enter the naval base to seize it, the French navy sinks its own ships so that neither Germany nor the Allies can have them. Seventy-seven vessels, among them three battleships and seven cruisers, go down in the harbour.
events.search: Scuttling of the French fleet at Toulon 1942

events.title: The liberation of Corsica, September – October 1943
events.summary: After Italy's armistice, the Corsican resistance rises and Free French troops land from Algiers, helped by Italian units now on the Allied side. The German troops withdraw to Bastia and leave on 4 October 1943: Corsica is the first French department to be liberated.
events.search: Liberation of Corsica 1943

events.title: Lebanon becomes independent, 22 November 1943
events.summary: Lebanon's new parliament removes the French mandate from the constitution. The Free French authorities arrest the president, Bechara El Khoury, and his ministers; strikes and protests, and pressure from Britain, force their release eleven days later. 22 November is Lebanon's Independence Day; the last French troops leave in 1946.
events.search: Lebanon independence 22 November 1943

events.title: D-Day: the Normandy landings, 6 June 1944
events.summary: More than 150,000 American, British, Canadian and Free French soldiers land on five beaches of Normandy, after paratroopers have dropped behind them during the night. The Battle of Normandy lasts until the end of August and opens the way to Paris and the liberation of western Europe.
events.search: D-Day Normandy landings 6 June 1944 Overlord

events.title: Operation Dragoon: the Provence landings, 15 August 1944
events.summary: American troops and the French First Army, largely from North Africa, land between Toulon and Cannes. They free Toulon and Marseille by the end of August and race up the Rhône valley, meeting the troops from Normandy in Burgundy in September.
events.search: Operation Dragoon Provence landings 15 August 1944

events.title: The liberation of Paris, 19 – 25 August 1944
events.summary: The Paris resistance rises on 19 August. General Leclerc's 2nd Armoured Division enters the city on the 24th, and the next day the German commander, General von Choltitz, surrenders without carrying out Hitler's order to destroy it. Charles de Gaulle walks down the Champs-Élysées on 26 August.
events.search: Liberation of Paris 25 August 1944

events.title: The Japanese coup in Indochina, 9 March 1945
events.place: Huế and the whole of Indochina
events.summary: Expecting an Allied landing, Japan overthrows the French administration in one night and attacks French garrisons across Indochina; thousands of French soldiers and civilians are killed or interned. Japan has Emperor Bảo Đại proclaim an "Empire of Vietnam" in Huế, and the kings of Cambodia and Laos declare independence.
events.search: Japanese coup d'etat French Indochina 9 March 1945 Empire of Vietnam

events.title: The Levant crisis, May – June 1945
events.summary: France lands more troops in Syria and Lebanon to keep its influence there. Protests turn into fighting, and on 29 May French artillery and planes shell Damascus, killing hundreds. Churchill threatens to intervene, British troops step in and the French are confined to their barracks; the last French troops leave Syria in April 1946 and Lebanon in December 1946.
events.search: Levant Crisis 1945 Damascus bombardment

events.title: Guangzhouwan returns to China, 18 August 1945
events.summary: Leased to France in 1898 and run from Hanoi as part of French Indochina, the territory around Zhanjiang bay was occupied by Japan in February 1943. Three days after Japan's surrender, France agrees to give it back to the Republic of China. The town of Fort-Bayard becomes Zhanjiang.
events.search: Guangzhouwan Kouang-Tcheou-Wan returned to China 1945

events.title: Hồ Chí Minh declares Vietnam's independence, 2 September 1945
events.summary: After the Viet Minh's August Revolution and the abdication of Emperor Bảo Đại, Hồ Chí Minh reads the declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam before a huge crowd in Hanoi. France does not accept it: Chinese troops occupy the north, French troops retake the south, and war breaks out at the end of 1946.
events.search: Ho Chi Minh declaration of independence Vietnam 2 September 1945 Ba Dinh

events.title: The Battle of Maysalun, 24 July 1920
events.summary: Faisal's Arab Kingdom of Syria, proclaimed in March, refuses the French mandate given at San Remo. General Gouraud's army crushes the Syrian volunteers of Yusuf al-Azma at the Maysalun pass and enters Damascus the next day. Faisal goes into exile, and France splits Syria into several states: Damascus, Aleppo, the Alawites and, in 1921, Jabal Druze.
events.search: Battle of Maysalun 1920 Faisal Arab Kingdom of Syria Gouraud

events.title: Greater Lebanon is proclaimed, 1 September 1920
events.summary: In Beirut, General Gouraud proclaims the State of Greater Lebanon: to the old autonomous Mount Lebanon, France adds Beirut, Tripoli, Sidon, Tyre and the Beqaa valley. These are today's borders of Lebanon. The state becomes the Lebanese Republic with its constitution of 1926, still under French mandate.
events.search: Greater Lebanon 1920 Gouraud proclamation Beirut

events.title: The Franco-Turkish War and the Treaty of Ankara, 1918 – 1921
events.summary: After the Ottoman defeat, French troops occupy Cilicia, around Adana. Turkish nationalists led by Mustafa Kemal fight them at Marash, Urfa and Aintab. By the Treaty of Ankara of 20 October 1921, France leaves Cilicia and draws the border between Syria and Turkey, keeping the Sanjak of Alexandretta under a special regime.
events.search: Franco-Turkish War Cilicia 1918 1921 Treaty of Ankara Marash Aintab

events.title: The Rif War, 1921 – 1926
events.summary: The Berber tribes of the Rif, led by Abd el-Krim, rise against Spain and crush its army at Annual in 1921, then found a Republic of the Rif. In 1925 they attack the French zone; France sends Marshal Pétain with a large army and, with Spain, which lands at Al Hoceima, defeats them. Abd el-Krim surrenders to the French in May 1926.
events.search: Rif War 1921 1926 Abd el-Krim Annual Republic of the Rif

events.title: The Congo–Ocean railway, 1921 – 1934
events.place: From Brazzaville to Pointe-Noire, across the Mayombe
events.summary: To link Brazzaville to the sea without going through the Belgian Congo, France builds a railway of 500 km to Pointe-Noire. Africans from all over French Equatorial Africa are forced to work on it, above all in the Mayombe forest; about 17,000 of them die. André Gide and Albert Londres denounce the work site. The line opens in 1934.
events.search: Congo-Ocean railway 1921 1934 forced labour Brazzaville Pointe-Noire

events.title: The occupation of the Ruhr, 1923 – 1925
events.summary: Germany falls behind on the war reparations of the Treaty of Versailles. In January 1923, French and Belgian troops occupy the Ruhr, its main coal and steel basin, to take payment in kind. German workers answer with passive resistance, and German money collapses into hyperinflation. The Dawes Plan of 1924 settles the payments, and the troops leave in 1925.
events.search: Occupation of the Ruhr 1923 1925 reparations passive resistance

events.title: Tangier becomes an international zone, 1 June 1925
events.summary: Neither France nor Spain wants the other to hold Tangier, which faces Gibraltar. By the Tangier Convention of 1923, France, Spain and the United Kingdom make the city and its surroundings an international zone, neutral and demilitarised, under the Sultan's nominal rule. It comes into force on 1 June 1925 and lasts, apart from a Spanish occupation from 1940 to 1945, until 1956.
events.search: Tangier International Zone 1923 convention 1925

events.title: The Great Syrian Revolt, 1925 – 1927
events.summary: The Druze of Jabal Druze, led by Sultan al-Atrash, rise against French rule in July 1925, and nationalists across Syria join them. In October, the French shell Damascus, killing hundreds. With large reinforcements, France puts the revolt down by 1927, but it has to promise Syria a constitution, granted in 1930.
events.search: Great Syrian Revolt 1925 1927 Sultan al-Atrash Jabal Druze bombardment of Damascus

events.title: The Kongo-Wara rebellion, 1928 – 1931
events.summary: The Gbaya people, worn down by forced labour, the rubber companies and recruiting for the Congo–Ocean railway, rise at the call of the prophet Karnou. The revolt spreads over western Ubangi-Shari and into Cameroon and Middle Congo. Karnou is killed in December 1928, but the fighting lasts until 1931: it is the largest uprising in French Equatorial Africa between the wars.
events.search: Kongo-Wara rebellion 1928 1931 Karnou Gbaya Ubangi-Shari forced labour

events.title: The Yên Bái mutiny, 10 February 1930
events.summary: Vietnamese soldiers of the French colonial army, urged on by the Vietnamese Nationalist Party, rise at night against their French officers at Yên Bái, in Tonkin. The mutiny fails within hours. The French crush the party; its leader Nguyễn Thái Học and twelve companions are guillotined. The independence movement passes to the communists of Hồ Chí Minh.
events.search: Yen Bai mutiny 1930 VNQDD Nguyen Thai Hoc Tonkin

events.title: Upper Volta is divided, 5 September 1932
events.summary: To save money in the Great Depression, France dissolves the colony of Upper Volta, created in 1919. Its land is shared out between Ivory Coast, which takes most of it with Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso to supply workers for its plantations, French Sudan and Niger. The Mossi chiefs campaign for its return, and Upper Volta is re-created in 1947.
events.search: Upper Volta dissolved 1932 Ivory Coast French Sudan Niger

events.title: Spain takes possession of Ifni, April 1934
events.summary: Morocco promised Spain a fishing post on this coast in 1860, and France recognised Ifni as Spanish in 1912, but Spain had never gone there. In April 1934 Colonel Fernando Osvaldo Capaz lands with a few men and takes possession of Ifni peacefully, after talks with the local tribes. Spain founds Sidi Ifni and keeps the enclave until 1969.
events.search: Ifni 1934 Spain Capaz Sidi Ifni occupation

events.title: The Saar votes to return to Germany, 13 January 1935
events.summary: The Treaty of Versailles put the Saar under the League of Nations for fifteen years and gave its coal mines to France. At the end of that time, its people vote: over 90% choose to return to Germany, now ruled by Hitler, rather than stay under the League or join France. The Saar becomes German again on 1 March 1935.
events.search: Saar plebiscite 1935 referendum League of Nations return to Germany

events.title: The Franco-Syrian and Franco-Lebanese treaties, 1936
events.summary: After a general strike in Syria, France signs treaties with Syria in September and Lebanon in November 1936 promising their independence within three years. The Alawite State and Jabal Druze are joined to Syria. But the French parliament never ratifies the treaties, and in 1939 France suspends the Syrian constitution.
events.search: Franco-Syrian Treaty of Independence 1936 Franco-Lebanese treaty Blum

events.title: Hatay State, then Turkey, 1938 – 1939
events.summary: The Sanjak of Alexandretta, part of Syria with many Turks, is made autonomous in 1937. Turkish troops enter it alongside the French, and on 2 September 1938 its assembly proclaims Hatay State. To keep Turkey on its side against Germany, France lets it annex Hatay on 29 June 1939. Syria has never recognised the loss.
events.search: Hatay State 1938 1939 Sanjak of Alexandretta annexed by Turkey

events.title: The First Battle of the Marne, 5 – 12 September 1914
events.place: The Marne valley, east of Paris
events.summary: A month into the war, the German armies have crossed Belgium and northern France and come within 50 km of Paris. General Joffre turns the retreating French and British armies around and strikes their flank on the Marne, helped by troops rushed from Paris, some of them in the city's taxis. The Germans fall back to the Aisne. Both sides then dig in, and the front freezes into trenches from the North Sea to Switzerland for four years.
events.search: First Battle of the Marne 1914 Joffre Gallieni taxis

events.title: The Togoland campaign, August 1914
events.summary: German Togoland is surrounded by the British Gold Coast and French Dahomey. British and French troops invade it from both sides in the first days of the war. The Germans blow up their great radio station at Kamina, which linked Berlin to its colonies, and surrender on 26 August 1914: it is the first Allied victory of the war. France and the United Kingdom share the colony, and in 1919 France keeps the eastern part with Lomé, today's Togo.
events.search: Togoland campaign 1914 Kamina radio station British French invasion

events.title: The Kamerun campaign, 1914 – 1916
events.summary: British, French and Belgian troops attack German Kamerun from Nigeria, Chad and French Equatorial Africa. Douala falls in September 1914, and France takes back New Cameroon, the lands it had given Germany in 1911. After a long war in the forest, the Germans leave Yaoundé in January 1916 and cross into Spanish Guinea; the last fort, Mora, surrenders in February. France and the United Kingdom share Kamerun, France taking the larger eastern part.
events.search: Kamerun campaign 1914 1916 Douala Yaounde Mora Neukamerun

events.title: The Zaian War, 1914 – 1921
events.summary: In 1914 France takes Khénifra, the stronghold of the Zayanes, a Berber confederation of the Middle Atlas led by Mouha ou Hammou Zayani. In November, at El Herri, the Berbers kill over 600 French soldiers. Although France needs its troops in Europe, General Lyautey holds on to his posts in Morocco throughout the world war. Mouha ou Hammou is killed in 1921, and most Zayanes then submit.
events.search: Zaian War 1914 1921 Mouha ou Hammou Zayani Khenifra El Herri Lyautey

events.title: The Volta-Bani War, 1915 – 1916
events.place: Around Dédougou, between the Volta and the Bani
events.summary: In November 1915, villages of the Marka and Bwa peoples rise against French rule, its taxes and the forced recruitment of soldiers for the war in Europe. The revolt spreads over the land between the Black Volta and the Bani rivers, in today's Burkina Faso and Mali. It is the largest uprising French West Africa ever saw: France needs a year and several columns to crush it, burning villages, and tens of thousands die. To rule the region more closely, France creates the colony of Upper Volta in 1919.
events.search: Volta-Bani War 1915 1916 anti-colonial uprising conscription Bona Dedougou

events.title: The Battle of Verdun, 21 February – 18 December 1916
events.summary: The German army attacks the fortress city of Verdun, hoping to bleed the French army white. Under General Pétain, France holds on, feeding the battle along a single road from Bar-le-Duc, the Sacred Way, and rotating almost all its divisions through it. After ten months, the French retake the forts of Douaumont and Vaux and the front is back almost where it started. About 300,000 soldiers are dead. Verdun becomes the symbol of the war in France.
events.search: Battle of Verdun 1916 Douaumont Petain Voie Sacree

events.title: The Battle of the Somme, 1 July – 18 November 1916
events.place: The Somme, between Albert and Péronne
events.summary: British and French armies attack astride the Somme to break the German front and relieve Verdun. On the first day alone, the British army loses about 57,000 men, nearly 20,000 of them killed. The offensive goes on for four and a half months, and tanks are used for the first time in September. The Allies gain only about ten kilometres, and the battle costs over a million soldiers killed, wounded or captured.
events.search: Battle of the Somme 1916 first day tanks Haig

events.title: The Sykes–Picot Agreement, May 1916
events.place: The Arab lands of the Ottoman Empire
events.summary: In secret, the British diplomat Mark Sykes and the French diplomat François Georges-Picot agree how to share the Arab provinces of the Ottoman Empire after the war. France is to get the coast of Syria and Lebanon, Cilicia and influence over inland Syria up to Mosul; Britain gets Mesopotamia and the land down to the Gulf. The Bolsheviks make the deal public in 1917, to the anger of the Arabs, who had been promised independence. It shapes the mandates of 1920 and today's borders of Syria and Lebanon.
events.search: Sykes-Picot Agreement 1916 Ottoman Arab provinces partition

events.title: The Kaocen revolt, 1916 – 1917
events.summary: With the help of the Senussi brotherhood of Libya, which is backed by the Ottomans and Germany, the Tuareg leader Kaocen ag Mohammed rises against the French in the Aïr mountains. In December 1916 his men besiege the French garrison in Agadez. A relief column breaks the siege in March 1917 and takes back the Aïr, with harsh reprisals against the population.
